title: O'Neil Spencer's breakdown on the Apollo stage
summary: Drummer Spencer, nervous and a heavy drinker, tried to reform on marrying, and one day kept drumming after the tune ended at the Apollo until Procope told him to stop.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Now, what -- did O'Neil Spencer have emotional problems?

Well, yes. Yes. Yes. He was a person -- he was uptight, tremendously nervous, and he had so many anxieties, and he used to drink a whole lot. Then he had what was a -- you could call it a nervous breakdown, you know. And it happened on the stage. We were playing the Apollo. That's another thing the Kirby band used to do, we used to play on the stage, shows, you know.

And Spencer, he had a very nice lady and he got married, so he made a complete about face. He wasn't going to drink anymore, he wasn't going to stay out late anymore, he wasn't going to gamble anymore, which worked in reverse. It backfired, you know, because he'd been used to -- he'd been living this life, you know, ever since he started in the business, I suppose. And it gave him a -- must have been some sort of a disease or something. It affected his mind. Because we were on the Apollo stage, like I started to say, and we were playing, everything was going down fine, and then he got to this number and at the end of the number, which he'd been playing -- this was about the third day into the week, and he got to this point where the tune was over and he just sat up there and kept on drumming. You know, so we turned around. Well, at first I thought that he was just going to do something, you know, like a little drum solo at the end, and so that was all right, go ahead and

do it, you know. It doesn't make any difference. But then I discovered something was wrong. So I walked over to him and I looked at him and I said, "Stop." I said, "This is the end. Stop." He said, "Now?" I said, "Yeah." And he stopped. Then the show was over and the fellow that used to work for Kirby, you know, drive the car and whatnot, he took him home. And that was the last I saw of him. And he died when I was in the army, in April of 1943 he died. No, '44. '44.
